children: Markets opened on a flat note Monday, with the Nifty 50 trading at 23,386.70, up 40.30 points or 0.17 per cent, against a previous close of 23,346.40 and an opening of 23,330.20. The Sensex opened at 74,535.18 against a previous close of 74,294.96 and was trading at 74,716.92, up 421.96 points or 0.57 per cent, as of 9.20 AM.
Top gainers at market open
IndiGo was the top gainer on the Nifty 50, rising 1.85 per cent to ₹5,011, opening at ₹4,925 against a previous close of ₹4,920, on volumes of 38,690 shares worth ₹1,928.73 lakhs.
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries advanced 1.31 per cent to ₹1,861.40, having opened at ₹1,832.20 against a previous close of ₹1,837.30, with 65,476 shares changing hands worth ₹1,213.19 lakhs.
Reliance Industries climbed 1.29 per cent to ₹1,242.20, opening at ₹1,234.10 against a previous close of ₹1,226.40, on heavy volumes of 7,79,959 shares worth ₹9,671.57 lakhs.
HDFC Life Insurance rose 1.17 per cent to ₹557.40 from a previous close of ₹550.95, with 94,094 shares traded worth ₹522.33 lakhs.
Max Healthcare gained 0.95 per cent to ₹1,059.30 against a previous close of ₹1,049.30, on 73,838 shares worth ₹780.95 lakhs.
Top losers at market open
Adani Ports was the biggest loser, falling 2.90 per cent to ₹1,771.10 against a previous close of ₹1,824, on volumes of 3,82,762 shares worth ₹6,819.59 lakhs.
Bharti Airtel slipped 2.37 per cent to ₹1,848.50 from a previous close of ₹1,893.30, with 8,24,583 shares traded worth ₹15,237.30 lakhs, the highest value among losers.
Wipro declined 1.56 per cent to ₹164.23 against a previous close of ₹166.83, on 9,77,783 shares worth ₹1,605.03 lakhs.
Bajaj Finance fell 1.11 per cent to ₹1,028.80 from ₹1,040.30, on 2,23,788 shares worth ₹2,304.77 lakhs.
Apollo Hospitals eased 1.07 per cent to ₹8,849 against a previous close of ₹8,944.50, on 9,432 shares worth ₹835.30 lakhs.
What do analysts say?
Analysts flagged 23,400–23,500 as immediate resistance for the Nifty, with support at 23,100–23,200. "Immediate resistance now lies at 23,360, with a stronger positional resistance near 23,600.

On the downside, the 23,070–23,100 band remains the key support zone," said Devarsh Vakil, Head of Prime Research at HDFC Securities. On Bank Nifty, Vakil noted it formed a bullish candle in the previous session, with support at 55,800–56,000 and resistance at 56,800–57,000.

Choice Broking's technical analyst Hitesh Tailor noted India VIX easing to 11.3850 with the PCR at 0.98. "Sustained buying above resistance could improve momentum, whereas failure to hold support may keep the recovery vulnerable," he said.

Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, urged a large-cap focus: "GDP growth of 7 per cent and Nifty earnings growth of 12 to 14 per cent are achievable in FY27... investors should wait for this pivot and, meanwhile, accumulate high quality large-caps available at attractive valuations."

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, cautioned that geopolitical risks remain a live threat: "Tehran has threatened painful retaliation against the U.S. any renewed escalation could quickly trigger volatility across crude oil, currencies and global equities.”
Wall Street ralllies after lower crude oil prices

Wall Street rallied in the prior session, with the Nasdaq jumping 1.7 per cent, the S&P 500 gaining 1.1 per cent and the Dow rising 0.6 per cent, driven by easing Treasury yields and softer oil prices.
The 10-year US Treasury yield stood near 4.93 per cent, while Brent crude slipped to around $102 a barrel. US initial jobless claims fell to 196,000 against expectations of 206,000.
FIIs turn into buyers
Foreign institutional investors turned net buyers on September 18, purchasing ₹599 crore in equities, breaking a seven-session selling streak.
Domestic institutional investors continued supporting the market with purchases exceeding ₹1,000 crore.
The rupee closed at 95.93, gaining 3 paise after the Reserve Bank of India intervened to defend the currency against early pressure from a hawkish Fed and weak Asian FX sentiment.

title: Nifty opens flat as gainers battle geopolitical headwinds
